object_description: two separate buildings set on platforms of different levels, a main school and a smaller annex
geometry_property: scale similar to the surrounding buildings
windmill plan around a top-lit central staircase
design_condition: the two buildings are easily installed on the topography through platforms of different levels, revealing a high plateau and a low plateau that hold the school square and the village square

positive: The two buildings are easily installed on the topography of the site
With a scale similar to the other buildings and delicately arranged to preserve the views
The complex succeeds remarkably in becoming one with the buildings of this part of the village
The integration into the existing topography through platforms of different levels is appreciated
The built volumes reveal a high plateau and a low plateau holding school square and village square
These are part of a series of places each marked by a large tree with fountain, bench or playground
This sequence of public spaces is a precise and sensitive connection between the site accesses
The stabilised gravel surfaces increase readability
The street furniture is adapted to the scale of the village
The varied plots encourage different modes of appropriation by time, day or season
The quality collaboration between architects and landscape architects was highly appreciated
The school is organised into half-levels with two undercover entrances, one per square
The bi-oriented classes turn like a mill around the central staircase lit overhead
A storage bench under the windows frees the other two classroom walls
This allows flexibility in layout lengthwise or widthwise
The annex could be enlarged in an extension without distorting the site
The timber structure on a concrete basement presents great rationality for vertical load recovery
Horizontal loads are distributed evenly
A fully wooden load-bearing floor increases the proportion of this material in the work
The fire protection solution is rational and easily allows a wood solution
The project uses the local forest owner own wood broadly but rationally
The project commits to sustainable architecture with local craftsmanship at the forefront
Simple solutions with sustainable materials, low-tech installations and low topographical impact
The jury appreciated the sensitivity and delicacy with which the project completes the village structure
It turns the constraints of the site into assets and creates high quality places in harmony with the existing
negative: The existence of half-levels slightly complicates the structure
The thermal inertia of the classrooms must be checked to avoid summer overheating
The light low-slope roof has a valley over its entire width requiring special attention
The absence of eaves exposes the facade to very strong weather stress
The small cladding elements must therefore be studied carefully
The stairwell details and its extension through the covered courtyards must be carefully worked out
